blocks.x: Claims triage in minutes — 55% faster cycle times with document intelligence
A top-5 global P&C insurer — Insurance & Risk engagement delivered by a 26-person team over 16 months, Global scope, commercial model: outcome-linked.

items: FNOL packets, estimates and medical files arrived unstructured; triage queues held claims for days.
Straight-through rates below 20% on simple claims; adjusters spent time typing, not deciding.
Fraud signals arrived after settlement; SIU capacity wasted on low-value leads.

blocks.x: We deployed the claims decision pipeline: document intelligence (classification, extraction, validation) feeding EEMS Platform decision policies with confidence-threshold routing, network fraud analytics scoring claims pre-settlement, and a portfolio lakehouse unifying exposure and claims for steering. Adjusters work a review queue of pre-assembled cases with citations.
A top-5 global P&C insurer uses the standard Achala delivery pattern — nothing bespoke about the governance, everything bespoke about the design. That split is deliberate.

items: Current programs land 70% here; the gate reviews the live number, not a projection
The delta we sign up to is down 52 — verified against live data at every gate

blocks.x: Towers: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation, Applied AI & Generative AI, Data, Analytics & Lakehouse. Platforms: KYC Management System, EEMS Platform, Fleet Management System.

items: What moved unchanged between sectors, and why it was safe to move — stated plainly.
What does not transfer between estates, and the adaptation it needs — named before the pilot, not after.

blocks.x: Anonymity is contractual; the measurement discipline is not — the same gates and evidence standards apply on every engagement.
